source.text: ወርኢኩ፡ ጽሑፈ፡ በላዕሌሆሙ፡ እስመ፡ ትውልድ፡ እምትውልድ፡ ትእብስ፡ እስከ፡ ትትነሣእ፡ ትውልደ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወአበሳ፡ ትትሐጐል፡ ወኃጢአት፡ ትትሰሐስ፡ እምዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወኵሉ፡ ሠናይ፡ ይመጽእ፡ ዲቤሃ።

translation.text: I saw it written concerning them that one generation will grow worse than another until a generation of righteousness arises. Transgression will be destroyed, sin will be wiped away from the earth, and every good thing will come upon it.

source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ ወልድየ፡ ሖር፡ እይድዖ፡ ለ*ወልድከ፡ ላሜክ፡ እስመ፡ ዝወልድ፡ ዘተወልደ፡ ወልደ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ውእቱ፡ አማን፡ ወአኮኒ፡ ሐሰተ።

translation.text: Now, my son, go and tell your son Lamech that this child who has been born is indeed his son; it is true, not false.

source.text: ወ*ሶበ፡ ሰምዐ፡ ማቱሳላ፡ ነገረ፡ አቡሁ፡ ሄኖክ፡ እስመ፡ በኅቡእ፡ አርአዮ፡ *ኵሎ፡ ግብረ፡ ወገብአ፡ ወአርአዮ፡ ወሰመዮ፡ ስሞ፡ ለ*ዝኩ፡ ወልድ፡ ኖኅ፡ እስመ፡ ውእቱ፡ †ያስተፌሥሖ፡ ለምድር፡ እምኵሉ፡ ሐጕላ።

translation.text: When Methuselah heard the words of his father Enoch, who had secretly shown him all these works, he returned and made them known to him.[a] He named that child Noah, because he would bring comfort to the earth from all its destruction.[b]

footnotes.text: The return and making-known clauses use unexpressed subjects and recipients. The English does not insert a named recipient or silently transfer the naming action to a different explicitly named person.

The printed dagger marks the comfort/gladden verb as corrupt. Dillmann1865 column1349 supports consolation and expressly cites107:3 with a from-phrase. Charles1906 printed223 note26 proposes a different underlying verb meaning grant rest and a Noah wordplay; that reconstruction is reported, not silently substituted into the selected source.

source.text: ወኮነ፡ እምድኅረ*ዝ፡ ተለዓለ፡ ስሙ፡ ሕያው፡ *በኀቤሁ፡ ለውእቱ፡ ወልደ፡ እጓለ፡ እመሕያው፡ ወበኀበ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ እምእለ፡ የኃድሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ።

translation.text: After this his name, while he lived, was raised up before him, to that Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits, from among those who dwell upon the dry land.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected wording is compressed: his name, living, followed by before/in his presence and to that Son of Man. The pronoun’s referent and the precise relation of living are not supplied by a new identity claim. Son of Man renders the extended human idiom in the printed Ge’ez. The third-person wording here and in verse2 is retained rather than harmonized to the first person of verse3.

source.text: ወተለዓለ፡ በሰረገላተ፡ መንፈስ፡ ወወፅአ፡ ስም፡ በማእከሎሙ።

translation.text: He was raised up in chariots of spirit,[a] and the name went out among them.[b]

footnotes.text: Or chariots of wind. The noun can denote spirit or wind; this phrase does not explicitly name the Holy Spirit. Dillmann1865 columns347-348 gives the vehicle/chariot noun, including plural forms that can also be used collectively.
The selected print has name without an attached possessive suffix. Went out among them preserves the movement expression without silently replacing it with disappeared or adding a missing possessive.

source.text: ወእምይእቲ፡ ዕለት፡ ኢ*ተሐሰብኩ፡ በማእከሎሙ፡ ወአንበረኒ፡ በማእከለ፡ ክልኤ፡ መንፈሳት፡ በማእከለ፡ መስዕ፡ ወዐረብ፡ በኀበ፡ ነሥኡ፡ አሕባለ፡ መላእክት፡ ከመ፡ ይስፍሩ፡ ሊተ፡ መካነ፡ ለኅሩያን፡ ወለጻድቃን።

translation.text: From that day I was not reckoned among them.[a] He placed me between the two winds, between the north and the west,[b] where the angels took cords to measure out for me a place for the chosen and righteous.[c]

footnotes.text: The printed verb is reckoned/counted, supported by Dillmann1865 column91. Charles printed128 note4 records forms for being drawn/brought; the English does not substitute those readings for the selected verb. The printed shift to first-person I/me is retained.

Dillmann1865 columns708-709 supports wind for this noun and cites70:3; column180 gives north forመስዕ and column964 west forዐረብ. The repeated between construction is retained without pretending its spatial detail is more precise than the text.
Dillmann1865 column100 explicitly cites70:3 under measuring cords. The selected source includes for me followed by a place for the chosen and righteous; neither phrase is silently omitted.

source.text: ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ አበወ፡ ቀደምተ፡ ወጻድቃነ፡ እለ፡ እምዓለም፡ በውእቱ፡ መካን፡ የኃድሩ።

translation.text: There I saw the fathers of old and the righteous who have dwelt in that place from ancient times.[a]

footnotes.text: Or from eternity. The expression is retained as an indefinite ancient duration, not expanded into a more specific chronology or doctrine of personal preexistence.
